info.name: Karasu Auth API
info.description:
Complete API collection for Karasu Auth - Centralized Authentication Service

This collection includes:
- Public endpoints (auth: register, login, logout, refresh)
- Protected endpoints (session management, user management)
- Admin endpoints (RBAC: roles, permissions, user role assignment)
- Session tracking with device info and IP address
- Environment variables for easy token management

Setup:
1. Import this collection to Postman
2. Update the {{base_url}} variable to match your server (default: http://localhost:8080)
3. Run 'Register' then 'Login' to get tokens
4. Tokens and session_id are automatically saved to variables
5. For admin endpoints, login as superadmin (username: superadmin, password: Admin123!)
6. Use 'Get Active Sessions' to see all your active sessions
7. Use 'Logout' to end current session or 'Logout All Devices' to end all sessions

item.name: Authentication

request.description:
Register a new user account

Validation:
- Username: 3-50 characters
- Password: minimum 8 characters
- Password must contain:
  * At least 1 uppercase letter (A-Z)
  * At least 1 lowercase letter (a-z)
  * At least 1 number (0-9)
  * At least 1 special character (!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:,.<>?)
- Password must match confirm_password

Automatically saves user_id to environment variables

Login with username and password

Returns:
- access_token (15 min expiry)
- refresh_token (7 days expiry)
- session_id (for session tracking)
- User information

Rate Limiting: 5 requests per 15 minutes per IP

Account Lockout: After 5 failed login attempts, account will be locked for 15 minutes

Session tracking includes device info (User-Agent) and IP address.
Tokens and session_id are automatically saved to environment variables.

Generate a new access token using refresh token

Use this when your access token expires (after 15 minutes)

Automatically uses the refresh_token from environment and saves the new access_token

Logout from current session

This will deactivate the session associated with the refresh token.
After logout, the tokens will no longer work even if they haven't expired.

Use this when the user wants to logout from the current device.

Logout from all devices

Requires: Valid access token

This will deactivate ALL active sessions for the authenticated user.
Use this for security purposes when you want to logout from all devices (e.g., password change, suspected account compromise).

After this call, all tokens for this user will be invalidated.

response.name: Logout All Devices

request.description:
Get all active sessions for the authenticated user

Requires: Valid access token

Returns a list of all active sessions including:
- Session ID
- Device information (User-Agent)
- IP address
- Created at timestamp
- Last activity timestamp
- Expiration timestamp

Use this to see where you're currently logged in and manage your sessions.

Deactivate a specific session by session ID

Requires: Valid access token

You can only deactivate your own sessions. Use 'Get Active Sessions' to see all your active sessions and get the session_id.

This is useful for remotely logging out from a specific device.

Get current user's profile with roles and permissions

Requires: Valid access token

Returns:
- User information (ID, username, active status)
- Assigned roles with details
- Effective permissions across all roles

Use this to check what permissions the current user has.

item.description: Authentication endpoints - includes public (register, login, logout) and protected (logout all, sessions) endpoints

request.description:
List all users with pagination

Requires: Valid access token + user:read permission

Query Parameters:
- page: Page number (default: 1)
- page_size: Items per page (default: 10, max: 100)

Returns:
- users: Array of user objects
- total: Total number of users
- page: Current page
- page_size: Current page size
- total_pages: Total number of pages

request.description:
Get user information by ID

Requires: Valid access token

Automatically uses user_id and access_token from environment

Create a new user

Requires: Valid access token

Note: pass_phrase will be automatically hashed using bcrypt

Create multiple users at once

Requires: Valid access token

Note: All passwords will be automatically hashed

Delete a user by ID (ID in request body)

Requires: Valid access token

Request Body:
{
  "id": "user-uuid-here"
}

Note: This is a soft delete (sets DeletedAt timestamp). The request automatically uses {{user_id}} variable.

Update user data by ID

Requires: Valid access token + user:update permission

Optional fields (only include what you want to update):
- user_name: New username
- pass_phrase: New password (will be hashed)
- is_active: true/false to activate/deactivate user

Note: Only provided fields will be updated. Omit fields to keep their current values.

item.description: Protected endpoints - require valid access token in Authorization header

item.name: RBAC Admin (Superadmin/Admin Only)
Role Management

request.description:
Create a new role

Requires: superadmin or admin role + role:create permission

Note: System roles (superadmin, admin, user) cannot be created via API.

Automatically saves role_id to environment variables.

response.name: Create Role

request.description:
List all roles with their permissions

Requires: superadmin or admin role + role:read permission

Returns all roles including system roles with full permission details.

response.name: List All Roles

request.description:
Get detailed information about a specific role

Requires: superadmin or admin role + role:read permission

Returns role details with all assigned permissions.

response.name: Get Role By ID

request.description:
Update role name or description

Requires: superadmin or admin role + role:update permission

Note: Cannot update system roles (superadmin, admin, user).

response.name: Update Role

request.description:
Delete a role

Requires: superadmin or admin role + role:delete permission

Note: Cannot delete system roles (superadmin, admin, user).
Soft delete - preserves audit trail.

Assign permissions to a role

Requires: superadmin or admin role + role:update permission

Replaces all existing permissions with the provided list.

Remove a specific permission from a role

Requires: superadmin or admin role + role:update permission

item.description: Role management endpoints - create, read, update, delete roles and manage their permissions

request.description:
Create a new permission

Requires: superadmin role only (permission:create)

Permission format: resource:action (e.g., content:moderate)

Automatically saves permission_id to environment variables.

response.name: Create Permission

request.description:
List all available permissions

Requires: superadmin or admin role + permission:read

Returns all system permissions in resource:action format.

response.name: List All Permissions

request.description:
Delete a permission

Requires: superadmin role only (permission:delete)

Warning: This will remove the permission from all roles that have it.

item.name: User Role Assignment

request.description:
Assign roles to a user

Requires: superadmin or admin role + role:assign permission

Adds the specified roles to the user (does not remove existing roles).
Tracks who granted the roles and when.

Remove specific roles from a user

Requires: superadmin or admin role + role:assign permission

Removes only the specified roles, leaving others intact.

Get all roles assigned to a user

Requires: superadmin or admin role + role:read permission

Returns roles with details about who granted them and when.

response.name: Get User Roles

request.description:
Get all effective permissions for a user

Requires: superadmin or admin role + permission:read

Returns the cumulative permissions across all roles assigned to the user.

response.name: Get User Permissions

item.description: User role assignment endpoints - manage which roles users have

request.description:
Login as the default superadmin user

Default Credentials:
- Username: superadmin
- Password: Admin123!

⚠️ SECURITY WARNING: Change this password immediately after first login!

The superadmin role has all permissions and can:
- Create/manage all roles and permissions
- Assign any role to any user
- Access all admin endpoints

Tokens are automatically saved to environment variables.

item.description: RBAC administration endpoints - requires superadmin or admin role with specific permissions

item.name: Test Scenarios

request.description: Test with wrong password - should return 401 Unauthorized
Try to access protected endpoint without token - should return 401 Unauthorized
Try to register with existing username - should return 409 Conflict
Try to register with mismatched passwords - should return 400 Bad Request
Try to register with password less than 8 characters - should return 400 Bad Request
Try to register with password missing uppercase letter - should return 400 Bad Request
Try to register with password missing special character - should return 400 Bad Request
Try to register with password missing number - should return 400 Bad Request
Try this request 5 times with wrong password. After 5 attempts, account will be locked for 15 minutes. Should return 423 Locked

Try to access admin endpoint with regular user token (without admin role) - should return 403 Forbidden

First login as regular user (not superadmin), then try this request.

Try to delete a system role (superadmin, admin, or user) - should return 400 Bad Request

Set {{role_id}} to a system role's ID first, then try this request as superadmin.

Try to create a permission with admin role (not superadmin) - should return 403 Forbidden

Only superadmin can create permissions.

Note: First, create an admin user and login with that account, then try this request.
